extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal financial assistance (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, campus administrators, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX reporting and confidential employee rules
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and implementation guidance for who must notify a Title IX Coordinator about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, how confidential employees are defined and treated, and related requirements (training, study abroad, safety threats, student-employees). Covers §106.44(c), §106.44(d), §106.2 and cross-references to other Title IX provisions and the Clery Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: K-12 non-confidential employee reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For elementary schools and secondary schools, require all non-confidential employees to notify the Title IX Coordinator when the employee has information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: K-12 employees exercise considerable control and supervision and are often mandatory reporters of child abuse under State laws; applying a uniform notification duty in K-12 implements Title IX's protections for students. See 87 FR 41437-41438.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postsecondary Category 1 reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: At recipients other than elementary and secondary schools (including postsecondary institutions), any employee who is not a confidential employee and who either has authority to institute corrective measures on behalf of the recipient or has responsibility for administrative leadership, teaching, or advising in the recipient's education program or activity ("Category 1") must notify the Title IX Coordinator when the employee has information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category 1 is fact-specific and depends on the recipient's policies. Examples include employees with authority to institute corrective measures and those who provide aid/services to students whom students would view as able to redress sex discrimination. This requirement mirrors the definition of "actual knowledge" in §106.30(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Postsecondary Category 2 reporting option
rubrics_metrics.description: All other non-confidential employees who are not in Category 1 ("Category 2") must either (A) notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, or (B) provide the contact information of the Title IX Coordinator and information about how to make a complaint of sex discrimination to any person who provides the employee with such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient may decide which of these two actions Category 2 employees must take or may leave the choice to individual Category 2 employees. The requirement is the same regardless of whether the informant is a student or employee; the Department removed distinctions based on the informant's status to simplify obligations and promote complainant autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient option to require universal employee reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient has discretion to simplify the notification requirement by requiring all employees (including those who would otherwise be Category 2) to notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an optional approach recipients may adopt to make notification responsibilities clearer and easier to implement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No departmental enumeration of job titles; recipient determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to enumerate all job titles covered by §106.44(c)(2); recipients must reasonably determine based on facts whether a particular employee is in Category 1 or Category 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should use a straightforward set of inquiries about authority, leadership, teaching/advising responsibilities, and the employee's duties. Because duties can fluctuate, recipients should update determinations and training when positions change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training when duties change and annual training
rubrics_metrics.description: Training must occur promptly when an employee changes positions that alters their duties under Title IX or the final regulations, and annually thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies §106.8(d) and addresses employee movement between Category 1 and Category 2; recipients must ensure timely training in response to changed responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee notification exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential employees (as defined in §106.2) are exempt from the notification requirements in §106.44(c)(2) and are not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator when a person informs them of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An advisor who meets the definition of confidential employee would not have notification requirements. The reference to "advising" in §106.44(c)(2)(i) does not change the definition of confidential employee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee required disclosures to persons who disclose
rubrics_metrics.description: A confidential employee, in response to a person who informs them of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, must: (1) explain the employee's status as confidential for purposes of Title IX and the Title IX regulations (including circumstances in which the employee is not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator); (2) provide that person with contact information for the Title IX Coordinator; (3) explain how to make a complaint of sex discrimination; and (4) explain that the Title IX Coordinator may be able to offer and coordinate supportive measures and initiate an informal resolution process or an investigation under the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement helps individuals access supportive measures without involuntary initiation of a Title IX investigation and promotes consistent information sharing; it is required by §106.44(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: First category of confidential employee: privileged or confidential communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The first category of the definition of "confidential employee" is an employee whose communications are "privileged or confidential" under Federal or State law; confidential status for Title IX purposes is only with respect to information received while functioning within the scope of duties to which privilege or confidentiality applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language was revised from "privileged" to "privileged or confidential" to encompass confidentiality protections that do not rise to a formal privilege (e.g., certain statutory or constitutional confidentiality). This clarifies the scope and limits confidentiality under Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employees not exempt from other legal reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential employees are not exempt from complying with Federal, State, or local laws that require disclosure (e.g., mandatory reporting of child sexual assault); disclosures required by such laws are permissible under §106.44(j) and not prohibited by Title IX confidentiality rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential status in §106.2 is limited to the Title IX regulations; other statutes (Clery Act, mandatory reporting laws, etc.) may still require reporting to persons other than the Title IX Coordinator. §106.44(j) permits disclosures required by Federal law or regulations and does not relieve institutions of other legal obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient obligation to notify about confidential employees' availability
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must notify all participants in the recipient's education program or activity of how to contact its confidential employees, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is set out in §106.44(d); recipients must give notice of confidential employees' availability while respecting any limited exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential resources vs. confidential employees distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: A "confidential resource" (referenced in §106.45(b)(5)) is not synonymous with a "confidential employee"; confidential resources may be non-employees and do not need to comply with the notification or disclosure requirements applicable to confidential employees under §106.44(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should distinguish between internal confidential employees (employees meeting §106.2) and outside confidential resources (e.g., community-based rape crisis counselors, clergy, physicians). §106.45(b)(5) addresses privacy protections around consultation with confidential resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study abroad scope and Title IX Coordinator contact information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must include the name or title, office address, email address, and telephone number of the Title IX Coordinator in the recipient's notice of nondiscrimination; Title IX applies to sex discrimination occurring under a recipient's education program or activity in the United States, but conduct occurring in study abroad programs is not governed by these regulations unless it contributes to a hostile environment in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may adopt procedures addressing conduct outside the U.S., but Title IX does not apply extraterritorially. See §106.8(c)(1)(i) and §106.11. Commenters' concerns about study-abroad contacts are addressed by the notice requirement and the limited scope of Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety threats reporting left to recipient policy and other laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to add a regulation requiring any employee to immediately report conduct that poses a safety threat; recipients remain responsible for responding to safety threats and may require immediate reporting of sex-based safety threats in their own policies; for postsecondary institutions, the Clery Act also governs certain reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations do not mandate immediate reporting of safety threats, but nothing prevents a recipient from requiring immediate reports. Confidential employees are not required to immediately report safety threats under these regulations, although they must explain privacy limits and contact info; disclosures required by Federal, State, or local law (including mandatory reporting) are permissible under §106.44(j). See §§106.44(e),(f),(h),106.46(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of employment discrimination under Title IX
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX covers discrimination on the basis of sex in employment in recipient education programs and activities; employment discrimination may also fall under the jurisdiction of the EEOC and Title VII, and OCR's Case Processing Manual recognizes overlapping jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites N. Haven Bd. of Educ., historical regulations dating to 1975, and OCR guidance; the Department will not remove employment coverage from Title IX regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Category 2 employees must provide (clarified)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Category 2 employee elects the alternative option, they must provide the contact information of the Title IX Coordinator and information about how to make a complaint of sex discrimination; they are not required to explain grievance procedures or supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text was modified for clarity to state "how to make a complaint of" sex discrimination. The Title IX Coordinator is responsible under §106.44(f)(1) for providing consistent information about grievance procedures and supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student-employee status determination and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution must reasonably determine and specify whether and under what circumstances a person who is both a student and an employee is subject to the requirements of paragraph (c)(2); the Department removed the proposed specific factors and left recipient discretion, but recipients should give notice to student-employees about the circumstances that apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because employment laws vary by State and institutional arrangements differ, recipients have flexibility to adopt factors or rules to determine student-employee status, but must communicate those rules to affected student-employees.
